explanation: In polar coordinates a point is given by an angle theta and a distance r from the origin, so a curve is r = f(theta) instead of y = f(x). The sweeping green ray shows the current angle, and r tells how far out along that ray the curve sits — as theta runs around the circle the radius pulses, tracing roses and limaçons. The whole-number slider k sets how many petals/lobes appear, a sets their reach, and b lifts the radius so the curve can avoid (or pass through) the origin.
bullets: A polar point is (r, theta): distance from the origin at a given angle.
k controls the number of lobes; with b = 0 an odd k gives k petals, an even k gives 2k.
b shifts the radius, turning a rose into a limaçon (inner loop, dimple, or cardioid).
